sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Extracellular HRP proximity labeling was functional, confirming the fusion protein reached the cell surface with the tag exposed on the extracellular face (L2). HA-tagged RNF43-WT construct was used in published functional assays (L1); explicit Wnt-signaling readout not stated in the clip.
sites.rationale: The signal peptide of RNF43 spans residues 1–23 (last residue A at position 23); the mature ectodomain begins at G24. L2 explicitly places HRP 'immediately after the signal peptide' in the full-length, membrane-anchored protein, pinning the junction to insert_after_residue=23. L1 independently places an HA tag at the extracellular N-terminus of full-length RNF43 using a CD8 signal peptide, which also resolves to the same canonical junction (after residue 23). Python confirmed residue 23 = A and residue 24 = G; the insert point is 176 residues from the TM boundary (199), well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. Full-length membrane-anchored RNF43 with HRP inserted within the ectodomain immediately after the signal peptide (residues 1–23), enabling extracellular proximity labeling; construct expressed in mammalian cells. L1 independently corroborates the same junction with an HA tag driven by a CD8 signal peptide on full-length RNF43-WT used in Wnt-signaling functional studies.

sources.claim: Using RNF43 as a bait, we generated two different fusion constructs: in the first, we appended the coding sequence for APEX2 at the C-terminal of its cytosolic tail (Fig. 1a) ; in the second, we inserted the cDNA encoding for HRP within the RNF43 ectodomain, immediately after the signal peptide required for RNF43 plasma membrane localization (Fig. 1a) .

literature_notes: L1 and L2 both pin a tag to the same junction (after residue 23, the SP/ectodomain boundary); they are reported as one site with L2 as the primary clip because it names the position most precisely. L3, L4, L5, and L6 all describe C-terminal tags on full-length RNF43; the C-terminus (residue 783) falls within the intracellular domain (residues 220–783) and is therefore recorded in other_positions only. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for RNF43.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag on full-length hRNF43 (WT and mutants) used in mammalian expression studies; the C-terminus lies within the intracellular domain (residues 220–783) and is not accessible from the extracellular face.
C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length wild-type RNF43 generated by PCR subcloning; same intracellular C-terminus as L3/L4/L6.
